I was looking through my collection and looked at Holy Wrath. I thought why the hell is such a cool card not playable. The amount of damage it will do is simply unreliable. Placing faith entirely on a draw is one of the main parts of card games that I don't like. Perhaps we can give at least SOME control over how much damage the card can do. So, I came up with this.

https://i.imgur.com/dpyqZWO.png [1]

Redemption - 2 Mana Spell - "Place a friendly minion on the top of your deck."

The card would work similarly to a Rogue's Shadowstep. But instead of placing a friendly minion from the field to your hand, it would go from the field to the top of your deck. In order to use both Redemption and Holy Wrath together it would have to be at least turn 7 (not counting if Emperor Thaurissan was in play). This is because if you don't play Holy Wrath the turn you play Redemption, you would have already drawn the minion you placed on the top of your deck, making the damage value of your next Holy Wrath a mystery to the next draw again.

https://i.imgur.com/MsKEFUo.png [2]

Redeption - 2 Mana Spell - "Give a minion 'Deathrattle: Place this minion on the top of your deck.'"

I considered that perhaps the first version would perhaps be a bit too fast and wouldn't give the opponent the ability to play around it. This second version gives the opponent the ability to play around the deathrattle. The strategy for the Paladin with this second version would be to sacrifice the minion with the deathrattle, sending the minion to the top of your deck, and cast Holy Wrath in the same turn. This makes it a bit harder for Paladins to utilize a Molten Giant's mana considering it's difficult to sacrifice an 8 health minion by trading.

How would this card affect the Paladin's play style? What changes would you make to the card?

NOTE: I posted this on Reddit originally but it got downvoted pretty quickly.
[Card Concept] - Giving Paladins control of their Holy Wrath

It's an interesting idea, but I think generally Holy Wrath isn't that bad of a card. I'd even go as far as to say it's probably around average in arena, maybe above average if your curve is top heavy. Because if you think about it, Holy Wrath lets you pay 1 extra mana to play a Hammer of Wrath that has the potential to do a lot more damage. So the extra mana cost is really just whether or not you think the extra [x] damage is worth it.

I like the second version of your card better because, like you said, it's harder to abuse with Molten Giants. I don't think having this card would make Holy Wrath viable in constructed since it would be way too situational. The card on its own is SUPER slow since you're trading tempo for value (like the opposite of Sap), which obviously means it can be awesome in a control meta and very poor in an aggro meta.

I really like the concept, however. I feel like it is very simple and yet can lend itself to be very useful in a lot of different situations.
